body.p: I. Introduction

Claims 1-20 are pending in this application. Claims 1, 17, and 20 are amended and claim 16 is cancelled. The amendments are made without disclaimer of subject matter, and the Applicant reserves the right to pursue subject matter of any previously pending claim in a continuation or divisional application. No new matter has been introduced. Support for the amendments can be found in the Specification, for example, paragraph [0128] and original claim 16. Applicant requests reconsideration in light of the amendment to the claims and the following remarks.
II. Rejection under 35 U.S.C. §§ 102 and 103

Claims 1, 2 and 12-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Garvin et al (US 2013/0196767 Al, "Garvin"). Claims 7 and 9 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Garvin in view of Volkov (US 2015/0375110 A1).

Amended independent claim 1 recites, in response to a second switching operation on the aimed target, switch back to display the aiming mark on the first virtual character in lieu of the third virtual character. Applicant respectfully submits that the cited prior art references fail to teach such limitation.
In the outstanding Office Action, the Examiner appears to contemplate the selected
object in Garvin as the first virtual character in amended claim t, and the next selected object in Garvin as the second virtual character in amended claim 1.

Garvin teaches that the game character may shoot and neutralize the selected object. Id. at [0049]. When such a change in the state of the selected object is detected (i.e., the neutralization of the object), the targeting display may shift away from the selected object. Id.

Garvin further teaches that the aim of the game character may be automatically adjusted toward the selected next object. Id. at [0051]. As shown in FIG. 3, the next object may be selected from the remaining objects in the defined focus area. Id. at [0050]. The selection of the next object may be based on the distance between the next object and the center of the focus area, between the next object and the focal point of the game character, or user input. Id. As seen, Garvin simply teaches the aim is shifted from the selected object to the next selected object, but fails to teach that the aim would be shift back to the selected object.

Indeed, Garvin teaches away from shifting the aim back to the selected object. The aim shifting from the selected object to the next selected object is triggered by the neutralization of the selected object. The person of ordinary skill in the gaming art would appreciate that the neutralization means that the selected object has been successfully shot by the game character and the game character would not expect to aim at the neutralized object again. That is, the aim would not be shifted back to the selected object that has been neutralized in Garvin. Therefore, Garvin fails to disclose, teach, or suggest, in response to a second switching operation on the aimed target, switch back to display the aiming mark on the first virtual character in lieu of the third virtual character, as recited in amended claim 1.
Volkov fails to fill the gaps of Garvin because its cited portions are silent on the

above limitation. For at least these reasons, amended independent claim 1, and any claim that depends from claim 1, is patentable over Garvin as contemplated by the Examiner, alone or in the proposed combination with Volkov.

Independent claims 17 and 20 are amended to recite similar features as the amended claim 1. For similar reasons as the amended claim 1, amended independent claims 17 and 20, any claim that depends from claim 17, are patentable over Garvin as contemplated by the Examiner, alone or in the proposed combination with Volkov.
III. Conclusion
In view of the amendments to the claims and the foregoing remarks,

Applicants submit that the pending claims are in condition for allowance. Reconsideration is therefore respectfully requested. The Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned attorney for the Applicants via telephone if such communication would expedite this application.
If necessary to effect a timely response, this paper should be considered as a

petition for an Extension of Time sufficient to effect a timely response, and please charge any deficiency in fees or credit any overpayments to Deposit Account No. 05-1323, Docket No. 514935.5001131.
